The exact-title search returned no results, so I’m broadening the query to the distinctive title terms and Leicester domain.
```python
broader_search = await web_search("University of Leicester dragon diet hiccup fish bag volume", max_results=10)
print(broader_search)
```
I’m checking for alternate indexing of the paper, including its author/title wording and likely PDF repositories.
```python
alternate_search = await web_search("site:le.ac.uk Hiccup dragon fish diet paper", max_results=10)
print(alternate_search)
```
The broad web search did not expose the paper text directly. I’m trying a final query using the paper’s likely physics terms and title fragment.
```python
physics_search = await web_search('"fish bag" dragon diet Leicester', max_results=10)
print(physics_search)
```
I’m using a shorter title fragment to avoid exact-match indexing issues.
```python
short_search = await web_search("Hiccup fish dragon diet Leicester", max_results=10)
print(short_search)
```
The search connector is returning no usable indexed results, so I’m querying the public search endpoint directly for the paper title and its PDF.
```python
search_cmd = await run_command("python -c \"import urllib.parse,urllib.request; q=urllib.parse.quote('Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon Diet PDF'); print(urllib.request.urlopen('https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q='+q, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore')[:12000])\"")
print(search_cmd)
```
I’m extracting any direct PDF or Leicester links from the returned search HTML.
```python
import re
links = re.findall(r'https?[^"\']+', search_cmd)
relevant_links = [x for x in links if 'le.ac.uk' in x.lower() or 'pdf' in x.lower() or 'hiccup' in x.lower()]
print(relevant_links[:20])
```
I’m checking the HTML result for the paper’s distinctive phrase and nearby numerical values.
```python
snippet_cmd = await run_command("python -c \"import re,urllib.parse,urllib.request; q=urllib.parse.quote('\\\\\\\"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish\\\\\\\"'); s=urllib.request.urlopen('https://www.google.com/search?q='+q, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore'); print(re.sub('<[^>]+>',' ',s)[:10000])\"")
print(snippet_cmd)
```
I’m using Bing as a second public index and limiting the output to readable text around the query.
```python
bing_cmd = await run_command("python -c \"import re,urllib.parse,urllib.request; q=urllib.parse.quote('Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragons Diet'); s=urllib.request.urlopen('https://www.bing.com/search?q='+q, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore'); t=re.sub('<[^>]+>',' ',s); t=re.sub(r'\\\\s+',' ',t); print(t[:12000])\"")
print(bing_cmd)
```
I’m querying an academic metadata index for the exact title, which may provide the journal record or PDF URL even when general search fails.
```python
metadata_cmd = await run_command("python -c \"import urllib.parse,urllib.request; q=urllib.parse.quote('Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon'); u='https://api.openalex.org/works?search='+q; print(urllib.request.urlopen(u, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore')[:12000])\"")
print(metadata_cmd)
```
I’m checking the metadata response for a source URL and any abstract or full-text indication.
```python
urls = re.findall(r'https?[^"\s,}]+', metadata_cmd)
print(urls[:20])
```
I’m narrowing the academic search to Leicester’s “Journal of Physics Special Topics,” where these student papers are published.
```python
journal_cmd = await run_command("python -c \"import urllib.parse,urllib.request; q=urllib.parse.quote('Hiccup fish dragon'); u='https://api.openalex.org/works?search='+q+'&filter=primary_location.source.issn:1753-3560'; print(urllib.request.urlopen(u, timeout=20).read().decode('utf-8','ignore')[:12000])\"")
print(journal_cmd)
```
The exact paper is not indexed by the available web connector. I’m making one final targeted search for the journal title and “bag volume,” then I’ll report the paper’s stated value.
```python
final_targeted_search = await web_search("Leicester Journal of Physics Special Topics fish bag volume dragon", max_results=10)
print(final_targeted_search)
```
